beats.say: A razor sells itself. And you never buy it.
Option one: a sleek handle, no blades attached.
Option two: handle plus a starter pack of blades.
Option three: the whole set, ready to shave.
In 1904 they shipped 90,884 razors but only 123,648 blades. Sounds generous.
But it does a job: it locks you into buying blades forever.
In year one they sold 51 razors and 168 blades - three blades each; the next year 90,884 razors with 123,648 blades, enough to keep selling.
You see it everywhere: a coffee kiosk sells a machine, then a pod subscription.
It also appears at a gym: you buy a bike, then a monthly fee for lock-in classes.
Because the subscription feels like the only way to use the bike, you accept the higher recurring cost.
Rule: watch for a cheap entry that forces future purchases. Follow for more.
